newsitem.title: YUGOSLAVIA: Yugoslav airlines JAT, Airbus discuss cooperation.
newsitem.headline: Yugoslav airlines JAT, Airbus discuss cooperation.

text.p: Yugoslav airlines Jugoslovenski aerotransport held talks with representatives of Airbus Industrie on Tuesday on possibilities for renewing JAT's fleet with Airbus planes.
At the meeting, the European aircraft manufacturer presented its offer of planes from the A320 series, JAT said in a press release faxed to Reuters.
In June last year, Airbus organised a promotion flight in Yugoslavia of its A319 aircraft.
"Renewal of the national carrier's fleet is linked with marketing the Yugoslav economy's potential in the world through compensation programmes as a means of payment for the planes," JAT said.
A decision on the choice of aircraft will be made by the end of the year after offers from both European and U.S. manufacturers whose planes are already in JAT's fleet are reviewed.

JAT last year announced plans to rejuvenate its fleet and said it was negotiating with Airbus, Boeing Co and McDonnell Douglas Corp, but that a decision depended on favourable credit conditions and on part of the deals being covered through compensation contracts with Yugoslav companies.

The Yugoslav carrier's current fleet of some 30 aircraft includes mainly DC9s, Boeing 727s and 737s and ATR 72s. Several aircraft are on lease to foreign companies. -- Amra Kevic, Belgrade newsroom +381 11 222 4305
